title: The lisse sheaf–representation equivalence
statement:
Fix the finite fields, prime $\ell$, algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and smooth geometrically connected separated finite-type curve $C_0/k_0$ of [d-real-setup]. Put $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$ and choose a geometric generic point $\bar\eta$ of $C$. Use the lisse adic $\Qlb$-sheaves of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. A lisse Weil sheaf is a pair $(\mathcal F,\varphi)$ with $\varphi:\Phi_C^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, using geometric Galois Frobenius and its actual etale adic pullback as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. No lattice stable under $\varphi$ is required.

Let $P=\pi_1(C,\bar\eta)$ and let $W=W(C_0,\bar\eta)$, with its degree map and a chosen degree-one lift $s$, be the Weil group, with the degree convention of [sk-d-real-weil], of [def-wf-weil-group, def-wf-fundamental-representation]. On the representation side take finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces with a $W$-action whose restriction to $P$ is an $\ell$-adic representation in the precise finite-coefficient-field sense of [def-pod-l-adic-representations](3); morphisms are $W$-equivariant $\Qlb$-linear maps. Equivalently the entire action has a model over some finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, continuous on the open profinite subgroup $P$, with $W/P=\mathbf Z$ discrete. Throughout, $E\subset\Qlb$ also denotes such a finite coefficient field, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_E$ as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $\gamma$ denotes the chosen degree-one lift $s\in W$, so that $F=\rho(\gamma)=\rho(s)$; nodes keeping the notation of this statement use these letters (the field automorphism $z\mapsto z^{1/q}$ written $\gamma$ in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] is $r(s)$).

The geometric generic fibre functor $(\mathcal F,\varphi)\mapsto(V,\rho)=(\mathcal F_{\bar\eta},\rho_{\mathcal F})$, with exactly the Weil fundamental representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] (continuous by [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation]), is an exact tensor equivalence. A short sequence of lisse Weil sheaves is short exact if and only if its corresponding sequence of representations is short exact on underlying vector spaces. Subobjects, quotients and subquotients correspond in both directions.

proof.text: Geometric hypotheses. By [d-real-setup], $C$ is connected and $\ell$ differs from its field characteristic, hence is invertible on $C$. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $C$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its only affine coordinate ring is a field, with only the ideals $0,k$, and its underlying space is a singleton. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. All the hypotheses of the adic clause of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] therefore hold for $C$ and $\bar\eta$.

Finite, integral and rational stages. For a finite coefficient field $E$, the rings $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\mathfrak m_E^n$ are finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Apply [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) at each level; its scalar compatibility identifies reduction on sheaves with reduction of representations. Clause (2), in the precise inverse-system, rationalized-Hom and common-field categories of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], supplies the resulting equivalence $H:\operatorname{Lisse}(C,\Qlb)\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_{\ell}(P)$, including full faithfulness, essential surjectivity, abelianness, exactness and tensor compatibility. Its action is evaluation of fibre automorphisms at every finite level. This uses the stated integral/rational dictionary, not surjectivity of transition maps between equivariant Hom groups. No derived inverse-limit assertion is needed.

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), (1.1.6); blueprint unit finite-level and integral/rational stages

proof.text:
The Frobenius twist and its direction. Set $h=\Phi_C$. Reindexing by $h$ in [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback] has inverse reindexing by $h^{-1}$, hence is an autoequivalence. Its fibre at $\bar\eta$ is the fibre at $h\bar\eta$. Apply [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] to $k_0\subset k$ (the finite field is perfect). The chosen lift $s$ supplies the specific finite path $\lambda_s$ with action rule $s^{-1}$. Extend it by [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport]. For every underlying lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$, this gives the natural linear isomorphism $L_{s,\mathcal F}:H(h^*\mathcal F)\to H(\mathcal F)$ and, for $g\in P$, the identity
$$L_{s,\mathcal F}\rho_{h^*\mathcal F}(g)=\rho_{\mathcal F}(s^{-1}gs)L_{s,\mathcal F}.$$
This specifies the twist without changing the choice of geometric Frobenius.

source.place: (1.1.10), (1.1.12); finite path convention as in the cited arithmetic-lift statement

proof.text:
Use the degree normalization of [sk-d-real-weil]: geometric Frobenius has degree one and the quotient is discrete. Construct the forward functor. For a Weil structure $\varphi:h^*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, put $T=H(\varphi)L_{s,\mathcal F}^{-1}$. Since $H(\varphi)$ is $P$-equivariant, the identity in step 3 gives
$$T\rho_{\mathcal F}(g)T^{-1}=\rho_{\mathcal F}(sgs^{-1}).$$
By [def-wf-fundamental-representation], every $w\in W$ is uniquely $gs^n$ and the prescribed extension is $\rho(gs^n)=\rho_{\mathcal F}(g)T^n$. Its homomorphism property and continuity are exactly [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation]. Thus the object map is the specified fundamental representation, with $\rho(s)=T$. In particular a general degree-one element $gs$ acts by $\rho_{\mathcal F}(g)T$, not always by $T$.

Morphisms and full faithfulness. For underlying lisse sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) identifies sheaf maps $u$ bijectively with $P$-equivariant linear maps $a=H(u)$. Naturality of the path from [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport] says $H(h^*u)L_{s,\mathcal F}^{-1}=L_{s,\mathcal G}^{-1}a$. Therefore
$$u\varphi_{\mathcal F}=\varphi_{\mathcal G}h^*u\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad aT_{\mathcal F}=T_{\mathcal G}a,$$
where the reverse implication uses faithfulness of $H$. Together with $P$-equivariance, this is exactly equivariance for every $gs^n$, including negative $n$, by the extension formula in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Identities and composition are those of the underlying fibre functor. Hence the forward functor is fully faithful.

Essential surjectivity. Start with a representation $(V,\rho)$ in the stated category and set $T=\rho(s)$. By [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2), choose $\mathcal F$ and a $P$-equivariant identification $H(\mathcal F)=V$. Use step 3 for this $\mathcal F$. The map $t=T L_{s,\mathcal F}:H(h^*\mathcal F)\to V$ is $P$-equivariant, since
$$t\rho_{h^*\mathcal F}(g)=T\rho(s^{-1}gs)L_{s,\mathcal F}=\rho(g)t.$$
Fullness lifts $t$ to $\varphi:h^*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$. Lift $t^{-1}$ as well; faithfulness makes their composites identities, so $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Its degree-one operator is $tL_{s,\mathcal F}^{-1}=T$. The reconstructed action agrees with $\rho$ on $P$ and $s$, hence on $W$ by [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. This proves essential surjectivity. For the equivalent common-field formulation in the statement, start with a finite $E$-model of $V|_P$ and enlarge $E$ by the finitely many matrix entries of $T,T^{-1}$. They are algebraic over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, so the enlargement is finite. The extended geometric model is still continuous and now stable under $T$, so the whole $W$-action is defined there; on each open coset $Ps^n$ it is the continuous geometric action followed by the fixed operator $T^n$.

Abelian operations on Weil sheaves. The underlying lisse rational category is abelian by [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2). The reindexing autoequivalence $h^*$ of [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback] preserves kernel and cokernel universal properties (apply its inverse to a candidate factorization). For a Weil morphism $u$, its commuting square with the two invertible Weil structures therefore induces isomorphisms $h^*\ker(u)\simeq\ker(u)$ and $h^*\operatorname{coker}(u)\simeq\operatorname{coker}(u)$. The inverse squares induce their inverses. These objects satisfy the kernel and cokernel universal properties among Weil morphisms: uniqueness of underlying factorizations forces the Weil-commuting square. Zero objects and biproducts receive the componentwise structures, and the underlying coimage-to-image isomorphism is a Weil morphism by the same uniqueness. This proves abelianness; forgetting the structure computes the kernels and cokernels.

source.place: (1.1.12), abelian operations expanded from the blueprint exactness stage

proof.text: Exactness and reflection. By step 7 a short Weil complex is exact precisely when its underlying lisse complex is exact. Apply the exact equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2): this is equivalent to exactness of the corresponding geometric representations on vector spaces. The additional operator $T$ commutes with the maps by step 5, so the vector-space kernels and cokernels carry its induced invertible action. Conversely those kernels and cokernels come from step 7 via the proved equivalence. Thus the Weil representation category is abelian with these underlying vector-space kernels and cokernels, and our equivalence preserves and reflects short exact sequences.

Paths respect tensor and unit. At finite coefficients a natural path respects products of finite locally constant sheaves of sets: naturality with the two projections forces its value on a pair to be the pair of its values. Apply naturality also to the underlying finite-set sheaf map $(x,y)\mapsto x\otimes y$. Under the tensor comparison of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1), the path on a tensor product consequently sends $x\otimes y$ to $\lambda(x)\otimes\lambda(y)$; these tensors generate. The path on the constant coefficient sheaf is the identity by naturality with its constant sections. The extension of paths in [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport] is by finite-level inverse limits, then rationalization and common-field extension; the tensor and scalar comparisons of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) therefore give $L_{s,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G}=L_{s,\mathcal F}\otimes L_{s,\mathcal G}$ and the identity on the unit. In the integral comparison equality is checked after every finite projection; rational and algebraic comparisons extend these equalities linearly.

source.place: (1.1.1), (1.1.12), tensor compatibility of the explicit path construction

proof.text:
The tensor structure is the actual one. The tensor product of Weil pairs has descent isomorphism $\varphi_{\mathcal F}\otimes\varphi_{\mathcal G}$ under the reindexing comparison $h^*(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)=h^*\mathcal F\otimes h^*\mathcal G$: the reindexing of [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback] is sectionwise along an automorphism of the etale site, so at each finite level it commutes with the sectionwise tensor presheaf and with its sheafification, and it is applied levelwise to the tensor systems of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Step 9 and the formula in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] give
$$T_{\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G}=(H\varphi_{\mathcal F}\otimes H\varphi_{\mathcal G})(L_{s,\mathcal F}^{-1}\otimes L_{s,\mathcal G}^{-1})=T_{\mathcal F}\otimes T_{\mathcal G}.$$
On $P$ the comparison is equivariant by the tensor clause of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2); the displayed equality makes it equivariant on $s$, hence on $W$. The unit goes to the trivial representation. Naturality, associativity, symmetry and unit diagrams are the underlying diagrams of that same tensor equivalence, so they commute also as Weil representation maps. This proves tensor compatibility for the specified stalk functor.

Subquotients. Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity identify monomorphisms into each object in both directions: the defining left-cancellation property is preserved and reflected by the equivalence. Isomorphic monomorphisms correspond, giving a bijection on subobjects. Cokernels from steps 7-8 identify their quotients; applying the subobject correspondence again to a quotient identifies subquotients. All short exact sequences are already matched in step 8.
